messages:
jordan: Quick follow-up on the ingress QoS refactor RFC — a couple of edge cases I don't think were covered. TL;DR: we need to pick where to enforce sustained vs burst limits (edge gateway vs runtime) and how to surface rejections so clients can fall back.

maria: Agree. My main worry is when Dedicated pools are saturated we'll start returning 429s from the gateway and customers won't see helpful signals; they need a soft-fail mode (grace queue or fallback to cheaper model).

sam: We proposed leaky-bucket at gateway + per-pod concurrency at runtime. That lets gateway drop spikes early but runtime protects node overload. Still need to define exact semantics for burst allowances and cross-tenant fairness.

jordan: Concern: bursts for new PLG customers (free tier) — we want short UX-friendly bursts but avoid abuse. Proposal: two-tier token model: sustained_rate (long window) + burst_credits that accumulate/decay. Burst credits allow small spikes without immediate rejection.

lee: +1. Also need fairness between tenants that keep long-running streams vs short requests. Options: weighted deficit round robin at runtime or priority queue with decayed weights applied at the gateway. Weighted DRR seems easier to reason about for tokens.

maria: Implementation note: easiest to roll out is gateway middleware exposing headers so clients get signals: `X-RW-Quota-Remain`, `X-RW-Retry-After`. Backend pods can set `X-RW-QOS-Proxy: overflow` to indicate a request accepted into a backend overflow queue. That gives support/debug signals.

ops-bot: :robot_face: deploy-bot: feature-flag ingress/burst-credits set to off in prod, enabled in canary us-west-2.

sam: small config prototype below (not final):
```
qos:
  sustained_rps: 2
  burst_credits: 20
  credit_decay_seconds: 60
  fairness_weight: tenant_weight
  overflow_queue_size: 200
  overflow_priority_ttl_secs: 30
```
This gives a soft backpressure path (overflow queue) before hard 429.

jordan: Next steps: 1) list exact metrics we need (serve_rps, dropped_count, avg_wait_ms, per-tenant-weighted-latency, burst_credit_balance), 2) run chaos/synthetic burst tests against canary, 3) document migration path from single-bucket -> two-tier, 4) update support playbook for Retry-After semantics. I'll open follow-up PRs and a short runbook for on-call. @maria @sam can you pick owners for metrics + canary tests? :+1:
